criteria.name: Mission concept and rationale — What will it do, who are the users, why is it needed?
criteria.reasoning: The mission goal, objectives, and quantitative requirements are clearly defined and directly tied to end-user needs (AIMS, GBRMPA, CSIRO, BoM). Relevant literature is thoroughly cited.

evidence.quote: Give reef managers direct, repeatable observations of coral colour over the whole Great Barrier Reef, so that bleaching is detected within days

criteria.name: Project plan — How you plan to complete the assignment, including either a Gantt chart or a timetable and information sources you plan to use
criteria.reasoning: The project plan includes a well-structured Gantt chart, task narratives explaining design sequencing, a comprehensive contingency table, and a detailed list of planned information sources.

evidence.quote: The main risks and the planned responses are listed in Table 1.

criteria.name: Preliminary progress — Technical content and evidence of sufficient work done to date
criteria.reasoning: Preliminary hand calculations for a 600 km sun-synchronous orbit are technically sound. The interpretation insightfully identifies the core coverage-swath trade-off against mission requirements.

evidence.quote: Interpretation: the reef is up to about 250 km wide, so a 60 km swath needs at least five neighbouring passes

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: The report is professionally written and structured, with clean formatting, clear tables, an effective Gantt chart, and accurate, consistently formatted reference citations.

technical_issues.issue: For a sun-synchronous orbit, ground-track shift between consecutive nodal crossings is relative to the sun-pointing frame, which corresponds to the solar day (86,400 s) rather than the sidereal day (86,164 s), though the resulting difference is minor (~8 km).

overall: An exemplary preliminary report that thoroughly addresses all assignment deliverables. Mission rationale, orbital calculations, project scheduling, risk contingencies, and presentation are executed to a high standard.

feedback.summary: You have produced an exemplary preliminary report that thoroughly addresses all deliverables. In Mission Concept & Rationale, you clearly linked quantitative mission objectives to stakeholder needs (AIMS, GBRMPA). Your Project Plan features an effective Gantt chart and robust risk contingencies (Table 1), while Preliminary Progress demonstrates sound orbital analysis and trade-off insights. Addressing a minor technical nuance in your orbit model will position you well for the final report.
next_steps: In your full mission orbital analysis, calculate the sun-synchronous ground-track shift using the solar day (86,400 s) rather than the sidereal day (86,164 s) to resolve the ~8 km difference.
Expand your swath-width trade-off analysis in Preliminary Progress by evaluating constellation or off-nadir pointing options to cover the 250 km reef width within the required revisit time.
Maintain your project momentum by tracking progress and updating mitigation outcomes directly against the milestones and contingencies defined in Table 1.

criteria.C1: Excellent work in Mission Concept & Rationale. You articulated clear, measurable objectives and directly linked satellite capabilities to end users such as AIMS and GBRMPA with relevant literature citations. To maintain this Accomplished standard in the final design report, ensure that all detailed subsystem requirements trace directly back to these primary mission and user needs.
criteria.C2: Your Project Plan is robust and integrates cleanly with your mission narrative. You provided clear task sequencing, a readable Gantt chart, and a thorough contingency matrix in Table 1. To maintain this Accomplished level in Part 2, track your actual task completion against these planned milestones and document any contingency plans you trigger.
criteria.C3: You demonstrated strong technical progress with your 600 km sun-synchronous orbit calculations and clear interpretation of the swath-to-reef-width trade-off. To refine your Accomplished work for the final submission, adjust your nodal ground-track shift calculations to reference the solar day (86,400 s) instead of the sidereal day (86,164 s), correcting the minor ~8 km discrepancy.
criteria.C4: The presentation is exemplary. The report follows a logical structure with clean formatting, professional tables and charts, and accurate citations that consistently match the reference list. To maintain this Accomplished standard in your final assignment, ensure that complex subsystem schematics, budget tables, and simulation figures match this high level of clarity and consistent styling.
